Title: New device joined your network
Recommendation: If you don't recognise it, change your Wi-Fi password and check your router's connected-device list.

Title: High-risk service exposed on a device
Recommendation: Open the Devices page for fix-it steps. Botnets break into IoT gadgets through exactly these services.

Title: Possible command-and-control beaconing
Detail: 192.168.1.47 contacts 185.220.101.4 every 300 s with very low jitter.
Recommendation: Many apps poll legitimately (updates, smart-home hubs). Look up the remote IP; if the device or owner is unknown, block it.

Title: Worm-like scanning from a home device
Detail: 192.168.1.47 tried Telnet on 46 hosts in 60 s.
Recommendation: Classic sign of an infected IoT device spreading malware. Unplug or isolate this device, then factory-reset it.

Title: Device contacted a known malicious server
Detail: 192.168.1.12 connected to a Feodo Tracker botnet C2 address.
Recommendation: Block the address and run a full Microsoft Defender scan on this device.

Title: Mirai BusyBox command [SIG-001]
Detail: Inbound payload matched a Mirai dropper command.
Recommendation: Check the device's firmware and change its default password.

Title: Unusual upload volume
Recommendation: Could be a cloud backup or video upload. If the device shouldn't be uploading (camera, plug, TV), investigate it.
